::: {.callout-note .legacy appearance="simple"}
This post is from the blog I kept as Preceptor in Mathematics at Harvard (2005–2008). It's kept here as an archive; some links are dead and references are dated.
:::

[![I Flock](http://spread.flock.com/buttons/I-Flock.gif "I Flock"){align="right" style="border: medium none "}](http://spread.flock.com/buttons/?user=&ref=I-Flock.gif)I’ve been using [Flock](http://www.flock.com/) on a trial basis for a while now. A friend told me since it was [Firefox](http://www.mozilla.com/en-US/firefox/)-based it would be faster on a mac. Plus he’s into all that Web 2.0 stuff that I’m still getting into. But I’m starting to get the hang of both.

Flock aims to integrate popular web sites and web activities into your browser. It has a blogging tool built in (I’m using it now). Along with the canonical bookmark (Flock calls them “favorites”) management utility, Flock gives a nice interface with your [del.icio.us](http://del.icio.us/) or [shadows](http://www.shadows.com/) accounts so you can tag pages on-the-fly. If you’re into [Flickr](http://www.flickr.com/) or [photobucket](http://www.photobucket.com/), you can use Flock to manage your photo collection.

It also has a nice clipboard of web “snippets” that lives in the bottom margin of any Flock window. So if you’re putting together a blog post and you want to copy an image from another location, drag it down there and then into anything else:

[![Photo of a physics demonstration](http://www.extension.harvard.edu/2006-07/images/crs_default.jpg){border="0"}](http://www.extension.harvard.edu/2006-07/courses/default.jsp;jsessionid=HCDFGJCBGFJF "Photo of a physics demonstration")

I guess your interest in Flock depends on how much you use these other applications. But I think it will be making it easier for me to blog, which is something I’m going to try to do more of.

**PS** I should give a shoutout to [Damon](http://damonjordan.com/) who was the first to tell me about Flock.
